items.title: Influence of traffic speed and acoustic environment on perception and perceived workload in virtual reality
items.summary: In a virtual urban park, 34 participants rated 30 km/h traffic as more pleasant and less eventful than 50 km/h traffic across three acoustic contexts. The context also affected both soundscape dimensions, while the measured difference in perceived workload was not significant.

items.title: The positive impact of naturally soundscaping a noisy urban space on same-night sleep in working adults
items.summary: A controlled field experiment added natural sounds to a traffic-exposed rooftop break area. Working adults in the intervention group showed higher heart-rate variability after the visit and into early sleep that night, but the difference was no longer evident the next morning.

items.title: Absorbing exceptional point of coherent vortex beams
items.summary: Experiments with acoustic vortex beams and symmetry-tailored metasurfaces realised chiral coherent-perfect-absorption exceptional points. Rotating the metasurface switched absorption capacity and degenerate states, while the vortex beams’ orbital-angular-momentum channels increased channel capacity and enabled sensitivity alongside robust perfect absorption.

items.title: Large language model-driven inverse design of acoustic valley-Hall insulators
items.summary: A two-agent framework couples a fine-tuned designer model with a manager that handles task planning, simulation calls, and multimodal outputs. Given concise bandgap requirements, it generates candidate acoustic valley-Hall structures, verifies their numerical response, and produces band structures, eigenmode fields, and manufacturable model files.
